subject.title: trusted-proxy auth: support fallback/default user when identity header is absent

question: Should trusted-proxy auth support an explicit fallback identity when a request comes from a configured trusted proxy source but lacks the configured user identity header?
rationale: The code change is mechanically clear, but it changes the Gateway auth trust boundary from per-request identity evidence to proxy-source plus configured principal, which automation should not decide.

options.title: Approve narrow fallback identity
options.body: Add a default-off single-principal fallback config with strict source/header/loopback/allowlist semantics, audit/docs/schema updates, and focused auth/control-ui coverage.

options.title: Keep fail-closed identity headers
options.body: Continue rejecting headerless trusted-proxy requests and document Cloudflare Zero Trust IP-whitelist or no-identity WebSocket setups as unsupported for trusted-proxy auth.

options.title: Require live Cloudflare proof first
options.body: Ask for a reproducible Cloudflare Tunnel trace before deciding whether OpenClaw should add a fallback identity surface.

recommendation.title: Approve narrow fallback identity
recommendation.body: Add a default-off single-principal fallback config with strict source/header/loopback/allowlist semantics, audit/docs/schema updates, and focused auth/control-ui coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is assigned, has already routed this issue separately from the local-direct fallback cluster, and owns recent nearby trusted-proxy auth policy changes.
